coverage.summary: Applies statewide to owners of residential rental property and their agents who charge application screening fees to applicants, including guarantors and cosigners. The statute states no unit-count, building-age or owner-type limits.
coverage.other_conditions: Does not preempt deposit and fee rules of federal or state housing-assistance programs.

evidence.quoted_span: (h) As used in this section, “landlord” means an owner of residential rental property.

(j) As used in this section, “applicant” means any entity or individual who makes a request to a landlord or their agent to rent a residential housing unit, or an entity or individual who agrees to act as a guarantor or cosignor on a rental agreement.
(h) As used in this section, “landlord” means an owner of residential rental property.
to preempt any provisions or regulations that govern the collection of deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.

result.notes: Removed the summary's reference to Berkeley BMC ch. 13.78 operating alongside the rule. No supplied document supports it: D005 is not among the documents, and the statute does not address local rules. requires_unknown_facts is set to false because the rule covers any owner of residential rental property; it is not limited to a class of buildings that assessor data cannot identify. The housing-assistance clause is kept in other_conditions as a non-preemption statement, not an exemption from coverage, so unverifiable_exemptions stays empty. All other fields remain null because the statute states no unit, construction-date, owner-occupancy or local-preemption terms.
